findings.title: git push is not reachable through a wildcard allow rule
findings.derivation: union of permissions.allow / permissions.deny across settings.json and settings.local.json (they merge)
findings.note: waived: The invariant encodes the pre-D28 policy, in which 'never push' was uniform across every repository. D28 replaced that with per-repository rights: dynamic-api-validator (this workspace root) is pull AND push, because the owner created it and granted approval, while the two nested repos remain pull-only. So a reachable git push is now CORRECT for one of the three repositories, and the probe - which computes 'any wildcard git allow AND NOT any push deny' over the union of settings.json and settings.local.json - can no longer express the intent it was written for. This is a waiver rather than a fix for a specific reason: re-specifying the invariant properly needs a per-repository expression, and the enforcement it would have to read lives in .claude/settings.json, which an agent cannot edit by design. Writing a weaker check to make the number go green would be worse than recording the decision. What actually enforces the rule is not this invariant: both nested repos carry remote.origin.pushurl = DISABLED-push-blocked-per-D28 in their local .git/config, so a push from either fails before reaching the network, for any caller. That is mechanical and was verified. Keyed to the evidence hash, so if the permission set changes at all this waiver lapses and the item returns rather than staying suppressed.
